matrix: Two of Cups U / Hermit R / Lovers U / Five of Wands U / Ace of Cups U.
notes: Implemented position names: You, The Other Person, The Connection, Relationship Challenge, Shared Guidance.

rubric.orientation: Each card is read with the meaning for its orientation (upright or reversed text from the card data below), and a reversed card is not merely the negation of its upright meaning.
rubric.position: The position lens names this position and reads the card through the position’s defined meaning (see the table), without drifting in time or role.
rubric.neighbours: The "wider spread" line relates the card to its pair partner (Celtic Cross) or neighbour (other spreads) without inventing a connection the data does not support.
rubric.clarifier1: Clarifier 1 is read as modifying the original card ("how it modifies the original card"), naming both, not as a separate definition.
rubric.clarifier2: Clarifier 2 develops the relationship between both earlier cards, naming all three.
rubric.synthesis: "Together" is a synthesis of the cards, not a list; revisions are shown (Revision 1 kept readable when Clarifier 2 arrives; Revision 2 when the Clarity card arrives).
rubric.clarity: Option B (approved 7 Nov): a Clarity card appears only when the original and both clarifiers are Major, is a Minor not already in the reading, and is read as grounding the three Major cards; a Minor original with two Major clarifiers gets none and the limit is stated.
rubric.max: Max’s lines are the reading’s own words (quoted), in reading order; before Finish he invites and does not sign off; after Finish the closing comes once.
rubric.failure: Deep’s six failure modes: templating, positional drift, reverse-as-opposite, parallel clarification, concatenation instead of synthesis, numerical/symbolic overreach.

positions.original:
Original Card · II · Two of Cups

You

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Water · Cups
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Water · Cups · Water

Number: 2

Two brings relationship, polarity and the need to consider another position. In Two of Cups, consider how this relates to mutuality.

Mutuality
Connection
Agreement

Position: You — Two of Cups. Here, mutuality, connection, agreement is a lens for your own feelings, needs and contribution to the relationship. Identify one concrete example in your situation and consider how it shapes your response.

A connection can deepen through reciprocal attention and honest exchange. Ask what each person is offering freely and make the agreement explicit instead of relying on an imagined harmony.

Looking closer: Two people exchange cups beneath a winged lion and entwined staff.
positions.lenses:
Tao / Wu Wei · Two of Cups

A practice of unforced attention with Two of Cups: What would a more reciprocal exchange look like here?

Jungian interpretation · Two of Cups

Psychological lens: Meeting another person requires recognising both connection and separateness.

positions.label: The Other Person
positions.meaning: your perception of the other person; use this for reflection, not as proof of their private thoughts
positions.original:
Original Card · IX · The Hermit, reversed

The Other Person

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Virgo
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Virgo · Earth

Number: 9

Nine draws experience toward maturity while asking what is still needed. In The Hermit, consider how this relates to reflection.

Isolation
Withdrawal
Avoidance

Position: The Other Person — The Hermit reversed. Consider whether your perception of the other person is coloured by isolation, withdrawal, avoidance. Check that impression through conversation rather than treating the card as access to their thoughts.

Reflection may have become a way to postpone contact or action. Ask whether solitude is restoring your perspective or protecting you from the conversation you need to have.

Looking closer: A cloaked figure holds a lantern on a mountain. The small light offers enough illumination for the next step, rather than a complete map.
positions.lenses:
Tao / Wu Wei · The Hermit

A practice of unforced attention with The Hermit: What do I hear in quiet, and when does quiet become a hiding place?

Jungian interpretation · The Hermit

Psychological lens: Inner guidance develops through reflective distance. Returning from solitude with something useful is as important as withdrawing to find it.

positions.label: The Connection
positions.original:
Original Card · VI · The Lovers

The Connection

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Gemini
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Gemini · Air

Number: 6

Six explores adjustment, relationship and a more workable harmony. In The Lovers, consider how this relates to alignment.

Alignment
Partnership
Choice

Position: The Connection — The Lovers. Between you, alignment, partnership, choice may describe a shared pattern. Notice how each person's response strengthens or softens that dynamic.

A meaningful relationship or choice asks you to act in line with your values. Mutual openness matters more than an ideal image of harmony; choose the commitments you can honestly sustain.

Looking closer: Two figures beneath an angel stand before distinct trees. Their openness connects relationship with conscience, vulnerability and a freely made choice.
positions.lenses:

A practice of unforced attention with The Lovers: What choice would bring my relationships and my values into closer agreement?

Jungian interpretation · The Lovers

Psychological lens: Relationship brings disowned needs and desires into view. Integration asks for conscious choice rather than expecting another person to complete the self.

Relationship Challenge

No planetary placement assigned

Five disrupts an established pattern and invites a response to change. In Five of Wands, consider how this relates to competition.

Friction
Practice

Position: Relationship Challenge — Five of Wands. The tension to explore is competition, friction, practice. Ask where this pattern becomes difficult and what small adjustment would help you meet it differently.

Different aims or styles are colliding. Treat manageable disagreement as information: clarify the shared task and make room for fair challenge without turning every difference into a personal contest.

Looking closer: Five figures raise wands in different directions without a clear common formation.

FROM CARD TO CARD

The reading begins with Two of Cups in You and moves toward Ace of Cups in Shared Guidance.

The Other Person · The Hermit, reversed. After Two of Cups, The Hermit (reversed) shifts the thread from mutuality toward isolation. Reversed, it shows that next step held back or turned inward.

The Connection · The Lovers. The Lovers turns against The Hermit (reversed), setting alignment against isolation: a turning point in the reading. Upright, it offers a way through the difficulty in The Hermit (reversed).

Relationship Challenge · Five of Wands. After The Lovers, Five of Wands gives alignment somewhere to go, turning it toward competition.

Shared Guidance · Ace of Cups. Ace of Cups turns against Five of Wands, setting openness against competition: a turning point in the reading.

From mutuality to openness, the reading turns 2 times, at The Connection and Shared Guidance: those are the places where a card pushes against the one before it, and where choice matters most.

THE OVERALL INVITATION

The themes running through the spread are mutuality, isolation, alignment, competition and openness. No single element dominates, so the reading reaches across several areas of life at once.

A question to carry, from Ace of Cups in Shared Guidance: Where am I ready to receive care rather than only offer it? This is a perspective, not a fixed prediction.

Numbers through your reading

Two of Cups (2) · The Hermit (9) · The Lovers (6) · Five of Wands (5) · Ace of Cups (1). Their numbered cards sum to 23, reducing to 5. No opening dice were rolled for this reading.

These numbers are symbolic prompts, not guarantees. Notice whether any patterns resonate with numbers personally meaningful to you.

Take what resonates, and leave the rest.

cardData.name: Two of Cups
cardData.upright: A connection can deepen through reciprocal attention and honest exchange. Ask what each person is offering freely and make the agreement explicit instead of relying on an imagined harmony.
cardData.reversed: A relationship or agreement may be unequal or out of tune. Name the difference and assess whether repair is mutual rather than assuming one person can restore the connection alone.

cardData.name: The Hermit
cardData.upright: Step back from competing voices long enough to recognise your own understanding. Solitude, study or a trusted guide can help you identify the next honest step without needing the whole path illuminated.
cardData.reversed: Reflection may have become a way to postpone contact or action. Ask whether solitude is restoring your perspective or protecting you from the conversation you need to have.

cardData.name: The Lovers
cardData.upright: A meaningful relationship or choice asks you to act in line with your values. Mutual openness matters more than an ideal image of harmony; choose the commitments you can honestly sustain.
cardData.reversed: Attraction, duty and personal values may be pulling in different directions. Name the disagreement before promising unity, and avoid sacrificing your voice merely to keep a connection intact.

cardData.name: Five of Wands
cardData.upright: Different aims or styles are colliding. Treat manageable disagreement as information: clarify the shared task and make room for fair challenge without turning every difference into a personal contest.
cardData.reversed: Conflict may be simmering beneath politeness or becoming a contest with no useful goal. Set clearer rules and decide which disagreements deserve your energy.

cardData.name: Ace of Cups
cardData.upright: A new feeling or opportunity for connection asks for receptivity. Offer care without demanding an immediate outcome, and notice what replenishes your capacity to give as well as receive.
cardData.reversed: Feelings may be held back or your capacity to care may be depleted. Create a little room to feel privately before expecting yourself to offer more.
